        - heading "Understand Derivative Graph" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A derivative graph shows f'(x), the slope of the original function at each x. In Derivative Graph, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Derivative graph: y=f'(x). You can learn Derivative Graph by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: Read the original graph's slope at many x-values. Plot those slopes as y-values on the derivative graph. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, motion: Velocity graph is derivative of position. Watch out: Thinking derivative graph is the original graph. It graphs slopes, not original y-values."

      - article:
        - heading "▣ Key rule" [level=3]
        - paragraph: The derivative at x is the slope of the function at that point.
        - status: f′(x)=lim h→0 [f(x+h)−f(x)]/h
        - paragraph: "Sign of f′(x) tells us:"
        - paragraph: • f′(x)>0 → f increasing
        - paragraph: • f′(x)<0 → f decreasing
        - paragraph: • f′(x)=0 → horizontal tangent
      - article:
        - heading "Worked example" [level=3]:
          - text: Worked example
        - paragraph: Let f(x)=x³−3x. Then f′(x)=3x²−3.
        - table:
          - rowgroup:
            - row "x -2 -1 0 1 2":
              - rowheader "x"
              - cell "-2"
              - cell "-1"
              - cell "0"
              - cell "1"
              - cell "2"
            - row "f(x) -2 2 0 -2 2":
              - rowheader "f(x)"
              - cell "-2"
              - cell "2"
              - cell "0"
              - cell "-2"
              - cell "2"
            - row "f′(x) 9 0 -3 0 9":
              - rowheader "f′(x)"
              - cell "9"
              - cell "0"
              - cell "-3"
              - cell "0"
              - cell "9"
        - paragraph: ● Zeros of f′(x) at x=−1,1 match horizontal tangents on f(x).
        - paragraph: ● f′(0)=−3<0 → f has a negative slope at x=0.
      - article:
        - heading "Common misconception" [level=3]:
          - text: Common misconception
        - paragraph:
          - text: "Misreading sign:"
          - text: If f′(x)>0, f is increasing (not decreasing).
        - paragraph: ✓ Positive → increasing
        - paragraph: ⊗ Negative → decreasing
